statement: On squared paper, P is 3 squares right of O and 1 square up. The paper is turned a quarter turn clockwise around O. Where is P now, compared with O?

choices.misconception: I turned the paper anticlockwise instead of clockwise.
I flipped P over an across line through O instead of turning it.
I made a half turn instead of a quarter turn.
I flipped P over an up-and-down line through O instead of turning it.

hints: Turn each of the two moves on its own.
In a quarter turn clockwise, every direction turns too: right becomes down, and up becomes right. Turn the walk from O to P one step at a time.
The walk 3 right becomes 3 down, and the walk 1 up becomes 1 right.

solutions.reliable: Think of the walk from O to P: 3 squares right, then 1 square up. A quarter turn clockwise turns every direction: right turns into down, and up turns into right. So the walk becomes 3 squares down and 1 square right. P is now 1 square right and 3 squares down from O. You can check with a clock hand: pointing right (at 3) and turning a quarter clockwise, it points down (at 6). The transferable idea: to turn a point, turn the path that leads to it.

whyOnTest: Turning a point about a centre by turning each step of its path is the basic tool for rotation questions.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
